highlights.title: Trump blasts decision that blocks mail-in voting executive orders: ‘This court has really let our country down’ – live
highlights.summary: The president called mail-in voting – which he has used on several occasions to cast a ballot – ‘a laughing stock’ across the world. Supreme court rejects Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections. Sign up for US Breaking News emails.
body: “The Supreme Court has really let our Country down! Certain Justices are petrified of these crazed and depraved Democrats, and are totally unable to show the courage necessary to save our America,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.
A reminder, only two of nine justices – Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito – sided with the administration. Trump called both of the conservative members of the bench “legends” in their dissent.

“This Supreme Court is bullied and cajoled by the Radical Left into making decisions that have set America back at least a hundred years,” the president added, while chiding the court’s decision at the end of its last term which also rejected Trump’s executive order which attempted to limit birthright citizenship and the earlier ruling which found a number of the administration’s tariffs unlawful. The president also accused the justices he nominated for the bench – Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett – not “the people I interviewed to serve” but “merely a shell of their original selves”.

highlights.title: What’s at stake in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble
highlights.summary: When Jessica Wachter, a finance professor at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School, wanted to assess AI’s impact on the economy over the next few years, she faced a long list of business and technical uncertainties.
body: Instead of trying to predict how useful and widely deployed AI models will be, she simply asked how fast the hyperscalers’ earnings will need to grow to justify their spending through 2027, when—she and her collaborator estimate—expenditures will reach nearly $1.1 trillion. It’s a no-nonsense accounting approach to making sense of today’s historical AI buildout.

The results are eye-opening: The AI companies will need to increase their own productivity by a factor of 2.7 to break even by 2030, accounting for the cost of capital and a 15% return, and depreciation of the assets. Not impossible, says Wachter. The result would lead to the kind of economic growth that we saw during the US IT boom over a period of about 10 years starting in the mid-1990s. But, she says, for it to happen by 2030 “that’s a lot of growth compressed into a few years.” And if the hyperscalers cannot meet such profit goals?

highlights.title: 'It's hard to understand' - what now for Russell amid Antonelli 'pain'?
highlights.summary: Nico Rosberg believes George Russell will currently be driven by a similar level of "insane motivation" to turn the tables on Kimi Antonelli as he was to get the better of Lewis Hamilton after recurring defeats.
body: Russell's hopes of becoming world champion for the first time this year are increasingly slim with in-form Mercedes team-mate Antonelli opening an 81-point lead over him at the top of the standings.

Since winning March's season-opening Australian Grand Prix, pre-season title favourite Russell has only twice finished ahead of Antonelli in the last 10 races they have both completed with the Briton seeing the young Italian take his seventh and eighth wins of the season across the Monza-Madrid double header.

Rosberg was asked after Sunday's race, in which Russell finished fifth, on Sky Sports F1 about his experience of rebounding to win his world title in 2016 after being soundly beaten to the crown by Mercedes team-mate Hamilton the year before.
"Subjectively, it was painful to keep losing against Lewis and that just drove an insane motivation.

highlights.title: Streaming's Best Spy Thriller Officially Confirmed To Return For Season 8
highlights.summary: Slow Horses remains the most consistent show on streaming. While many acclaimed TV series take long, multi-year breaks between seasons, this acclaimed spy series has released at least one batch of episodes annually since 2022.
body: The latest season will be based on the ninth and most recent book in Mick Herron’s Slough House series, Clown Town. The announcement comes shortly after Slow Horses ’ latest Emmy win, with Saul Metzstein taking Best Director for a Drama Series with season 5, episode 6, “Scars.” The show’s sixth season returns Sept. 16, 2026, and runs through Oct. 21, 2026. The upcoming season 7, based on Herron’s Bad Actors, was announced last year.

As for season 8, it “sees Jackson Lamb and Diana Taverner face off in their most explosive confrontation yet,” Apple TV’s summary reads. “When a botched attempt to blackmail the Park puts Taverner on the offensive, it is up to Lamb to unravel one of MI5’s darkest secrets and put an end to it once and for all."

Slow Horses is a darkly humorous espionage drama that follows a dysfunctional team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 known unaffectionately as Slough House. Oldman stars as Jackson Lamb, the brilliant but cantankerous leader of the spies, who end up in Slough House due to their career-ending mistakes and who frequently find themselves blundering around the smoke and mirrors of the espionage world.

highlights.summary: Exclusive: Correspondence requests state MP Melissa Horne to lobby on NextDC’s behalf – but contains alleged AI-created errors. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: The Victorian jobs minister has accused one of Australia’s largest datacentre companies of using artificial intelligence while requesting she lobby her colleague to approve a massive expansion of its “hyperscale AI factory”.

Correspondence between Victorian cabinet minister Melissa Horne and the chief executive of ASX-listed company NextDC, Craig Scroggie, reveals increasing sensitivity to community concerns about datacentres before the state election.

NextDC has lodged an application with the state government for fast-tracked approval to expand its controversial datacentre known as M3 in Footscray to cover 10 hectares, drawing 225MW of power and running 24/7.

The datacentre’s size and proximity to homes in Footscray has led to growing complaints from local residents, who argue the government has been too quick to approve developments without considering long-term impacts on the community.

highlights.title: AEO startup Profound hits unicorn valuation, raises $180M Series D 7 months after last round
highlights.summary: Profound has raised a $180 million Series D at a $1.8 billion valuation, less than seven months after it raised a $96 million Series C.
body: Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins led the round, and existing investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures and South Park Commons, also participated.

Launched two years ago, Profound started as an analytics platform, and has since expanded to help companies research and create marketing strategies. The startup helps businesses understand how AI helps consumers discover their brands.

It’s part of a wave of startups in the GEO/AEO space (generative engine optimization and answer engine optimization, respectively), where companies try to find ways to surface their products in the AI systems customers are increasingly using for search.
The company says its revenue has increased by 3x in the past six months, and it now has more than 1,000 enterprise customers, which include Comcast, The Estée Lauder Companies, and Walmart.

highlights.title: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 World Athletics Championships
highlights.summary: The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out.
body: Kenya has long been a superpower in distance running but has yet to host an event of this scale. The championships will return to Germany in 2031 with Munich hosting.

"We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council," said World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as he announced the decision following the Ultimate Championship in Hungary.
"The quality, ambition and commitment demonstrated by all four candidates underlines the strength and global appeal of the World Athletics Championships."

Jack Buckner, CEO of UK Athletics and co-founder of Athletic Ventures, said: "We are deeply disappointed that the 2029 World Athletics Championships will not be held in London. We believed we had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels.

body: Preorders for Metroid Ravenous went live not long after its standout trailer during the recent Nintendo Direct. There's been plenty of excitement since, and we've even seen preorders for the Metroid Ravenous Special Edition completely sell out in minutes across most retailers since the reveal.
But $10 off the standard edition of the game isn't a bad consolation prize if you were unable to secure a preorder for the special edition.

Yet, what's the deal with the immediate $10 discount at Walmart? Well, it's actually fairly simple. As is Nintendo's custom for this console generation, the MSRP for the game is $59.99 for digital copies and $69.99 for physical copies.

We've seen the same thing with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Star Fox, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Switch Sports Resort, among others. It's a pretty easy way to save $10 if you're planning to buy a physical copy anyway.

highlights.title: Can you freeze leftover risotto? | Kitchen aide
highlights.summary: It’s probably not a good idea to freeze cooked risotto rice, but if you must, we have three experts who can tell you how to minimise the mush. I have tried various ways to reheat risotto after freezing, but it always turns into a gloopy, starchy, unappetising mess. What am I doing wrong?
body: And, says Randall, if Jill “really has to freeze leftover risotto”, he would urge her to turn it into arancini instead: “Those work quite well, because you’ve encased the cooked rice in flour, egg wash and breadcrumbs, so moisture doesn’t penetrate the grains.”

And if Jill still wants to batch-cook, Poppy O’Toole suggests a shift in mindset: “The kind of rice that you can freeze would be baked [basmati] rice,” says the author of The Actually Delicious Batch Cookbook, namechecking a spicy chicken number that appeared in Feast a few weeks back. “That freezes and reheats beautifully.” Of course, the freezer is a fan of plain rice, too: “That’s a better way to batch-cook rice,” O’Toole says. “Freezing and reheating risotto never truly works.”

highlights.title: ‘In this new car, I feel patronised’: which driver assistance systems actually improve safety?
highlights.summary: Modern cars are fitted with features like autonomous emergency braking and fatigue monitoring. But do they support motorists or drive them to distraction? This new car I’m test-driving boasts all the latest bells and whistles – or, rather, beeps and bings.
body: When the car determines it’s too near a white line, it tugs the wheel against my hands and brakes as a car slows ahead. Its haptic “buttons” feel like fingers pressing back – as if an invisible presence has its hands and feet on the controls: a ghost in the machine I’m inside.

Heading back to the caryard, a cryptic tone sounds. From the back seat, salesman Anthony says it’s the over-speed warning. We’re still on the 40km/h service road but the car “saw” the yard’s 5km/h speed-limit sign. Anthony advises disabling it on start-up. “Most people leave it on, though,” he says. “Saves you getting done for speeding.”

But Anthony has turned off the car’s fatigue-warning feature. The car doesn’t “know” me yet, so won’t detect if I’m tired anyway. “It doesn’t like sunglasses, either,” he says. I’ve read about some systems that are so crudely calibrated they’ll insistently demand you take a break by confusing energetic driving on a twisting mountain road with drunkenness or debility. Others declare you unfit to drive if you’ve had a cold or a rough night. You’ve already seen yourself in the bathroom mirror. Who needs a robot to rub it in?
points: Modern cars are fitted with features like autonomous emergency braking and fatigue monitoring.
But do they support motorists or drive them to distraction?

body: On Tuesday, the PGA Tour outlined new membership categories for its two-tier promotion-and-relegation structure, launching in 2028.
Under the current PGA Tour qualification structure, the top 10 players finishing at the top of the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai Rankings will win PGA Tour cards for the following season.
However, the PGA Tour did not confirm how many cards will be offered to top performers on the DP World Tour.
The PGA Tour said: "Access available to top performers from the DP World Tour is being considered as part of the ongoing discussions regarding the future of the Strategic Alliance."

highlights.title: Sarah Pidgeon Nodded to CBK With Her Sleek Chanel Gown at the 2026 Emmys
highlights.summary: The “Love Story” star, who was nominated for an Emmy this year, made reference to Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy’s signature minimalism.
body: Ever since portraying Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy in Ryan Murphy’s Love Story earlier this year, Sarah Pidgeon can not escape fashion comparisons to her famed on-screen character. And it’s no wonder, given that CBK now represents the best of sleek minimalism from the ’90s—a vibe that Pidgeon herself often nails on the red carpet, via her own cool, sleek style choices.

At the 2026 Emmys last night, then, it was only fitting that Pidgeon nodded to CBK once again with her red carpet look —though this time, in a more subtler and more nuanced way. It was a big night for Pidgeon that demanded such a dressing spirit: She was nominated for the role, after all, for lead actress in a limited or anthology series or movie category. “It’s a pinch-me moment,” says Pidgeon. “With Carolyn, I had the challenge of embodying someone who’s so widely known, yet also very mysterious. I think our show offered a real recognition of the powerhouse of a woman that she was.”

highlights.title: Now Light’s minimalist phone can easily call an Uber
highlights.summary: More than a decade after its Kickstarter proposed a "cell phone designed to be used as little as possible," Light is adding a direct connection to Uber and Lyft with a new Rideshare tool.
body: The monochrome Light phones are adding access to rideshare services while still minimizing feeds and notifications.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

It’s an early preview of the LightOS “tool library” SDK that will allow developers to expand the phones’ features while still promising to minimize feeds and notifications. A blog post from Light says that “We’ll open up user submissions for the Tool Library by the end of this month, and look forward to having those available to everyone a few weeks after that!”

The rideshare integration works via a partnership with Tremp, which already operates an SMS-based way to order rideshares, and users set up access via Light’s dashboard website, just like other LightOS tools. It’s not free to use, however, as Tremp charges a 10 percent service fee with a $2 minimum, but it will waive that fee for the first five rides within 30 days of creating an account.

highlights.summary: Their startup, Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC) has raised $40 million in a Series A round led by Ribbit Capital, with participation from First Harmonic.
body: A day after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit his job over concerns that AI could kill us all by the end of the decade, I met with founders and brothers-in-law Rune Kvist and Rajiv Dattani. They think they have a solution that could save us all, or at least help prevent AI agents from going rogue inside enterprises.

“AI is getting smarter at an increasingly rapid rate. The surprising thing about AI is that it becomes harder to adopt and harder to control as AI gets smarter, not easier,” said Kvist, an early Anthropic employee who is also married to Dattani’s sister). Dattani is the former COO of the AI safety research organization METR.

The pair launched a startup called Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company ( AIUC ) that hopes to bring AI safety to enterprises and companies building AI models and agents. The startup names Cursor, Lovable, Harvey, and ElevenLabs as customers.

What caught the attention of this A-list group of investors is AIUC’s attempt to apply a familiar cybersecurity model to a new set of AI risks. The company has built a third-party audit and certification layer for AI agents.

highlights.title: Ian Schrager Goes Public: “There’s Nothing More Boring Than a Room Full of Rich People”
highlights.summary: As he prepares to open his third L.A. hotel — The PUBLIC — the Studio 54 founder and hospitality legend talks about his newly democratic door policies, getting ripped off by rivals and why he’s not afraid of failure.
body: The latest chapter is PUBLIC, built around what he calls “luxury for all,” and he is bringing it to Los Angeles inside a building freighted with somebody else’s mythology. The low-slung former motel at 8300 Sunset Blvd. was The Standard, which André Balazs opened in 1999 and ran until it closed in 2021. Balazs was Schrager’s erstwhile rival, chasing the same crowd through the boutique boom, and The Standard was his loudest answer to it: Guests checking in were treated to the view of young models in underwear lounging inside a glass fish tank behind the front desk. Until Schrager swooped in, the space had been sitting dark for five years.

He met me in the lobby in mid-August, trim and still cocky at 80, humming with the same restless energy that made him famous at 31. He is not a man resting inside his own legend. And best not to mention retirement.
“I sometimes think about doing something else,” he says. “But there’s really nothing else I like to do.”
You’re opening PUBLIC on the site of The Standard, a hotel lots of people remember very fondly. When you take over a property with that kind of history, do you try to preserve any of it?

highlights.title: Fast, furious and potentially fatal: why are supercars suddenly so popular?
highlights.summary: Once the preserve of the ultra-rich, supercars are finding new drivers through rentals, finance deals, influencer culture and the manosphere. But why would anyone want a 200mph vehicle?
body: Many of the supercars apprehended by the Met in August bore Middle Eastern number plates. It has been a growing trend for car owners from the region to spend summer in London, bringing their cars with them (at a cost of £25,000 upwards). The orange Lamborghini that Tatman seized had Dubai plates. Most of the vehicle owners retrieved their cars the next day after paying fines and presenting the correct paperwork. The Lamborghini driver was subsequently seen driving respectfully and not revving his engine. Lessons were learned, although the question remains: why ship a 200mph car to London to drive in a 20mph zone?

highlights.title: Is Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?
highlights.summary: When OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google DeepMind cofounder Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX head Elon Musk loosely agreed over the weekend to slow down AI development, skeptics spotted an ulterior motive immediately.
body: Major AI companies want to ‘pace the frontier’ — but their proposed solutions need real teeth.

The truth is more complicated, according to sources across the industry. The three-step proposal, laid out in an essay by Amodei, is calling for changes long espoused by AI safety advocates. While it could become a substitute for regulation, under Trump, substantial regulation is unlikely anyway. But experts say that on an issue that’s only likely to grow in importance, AI leaders aren’t the best people to lead the charge.

“The industry as a whole needs new champions,” said Nick Reese, an adjunct professor at New York University and the Department of Homeland Security’s former director of emerging tech policy. “We’ve looked at people like Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk as these people who are closest to the problem and working on it every day, and they’re the ones who know best. But the truth is there’s never been a realistic vision for what we’re building toward.”

body: Gabriel could have become United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup third-round tie at Old Trafford on Wednesday. But the Guardian understands he has asked for his registration to be cancelled.

United are unsure what has prompted this decision and believe they have done everything they can to show Gabriel and his family there is a pathway to the first team. Those efforts have included meetings with Ruben Amorim, when the Portuguese was head coach, and Sir Alex Ferguson.

United believe the situation, first reported by the Telegraph, is rectifiable given the time remaining on Gabriel’s contract. Club officials say the player has a deal to the end of the season and cannot be deregistered despite his request. The north London-born Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October next year, but can sign a scholarship agreement when he turns 16.

He confirmed this on September 13, and on September 14, Root won his first-ever Emmy award for his incredible performance on the show Widow's Bay.
body: In winning an Emmy, Root becomes just the second-ever Emmy-winning actor to appear in a GTA game. The first? That was James Woods, who voiced Mike Toreno in 2004's GTA: San Andreas.

Woods has won two Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actor --he won for Promise (1987), and My Name Is Bill W (1989). Woods also won a Daytime Emmy Award for playing Hades in the animated TV spinoff of Disney's Hercules.

Rockstar has not officially announced any casting details for GTA 6, but as mentioned, many people immediately recognized Root as the voice of Heder, and Root later confirmed his involvement in the game. It remains to be seen, however, who voices the game's two leads, Lucia and Jason, or any of the other main cast.

Root won his Primetime Emmy for Supporting Actor in a Comedy Series for Widow's Bay, an eerie, humorous show on Apple TV. He plays the central character, Wyck, alongside Matthew Rhys in the leading role of Tom.

highlights.title: LA It-Brand High Sport Hits the Gas with New York Fashion Week Teaser
highlights.summary: Five years in, founder Alissa Zachary is taking her fashion brand to the next level with a NYFW teaser and an upcoming store opening.
body: Five years after launching High Sport with a pair of $860 cropped kick-flare pants that became one of fashion’s most unlikely cult items, Alissa Zachary is ready for a bigger stage.

For spring 2027, the Los Angeles-based brand will join New York Fashion Week for the first time, releasing a digital lookbook that’s a prelude to what comes next—the runway. It’s a significant milestone for a label that has grown largely through word of mouth, without ever staging a party or press day, let alone a fashion show. And it comes as Zachary is preparing for High Sport’s next phase of growth, including category and retail expansion, creating a physical home for the brand in LA, and eventually, perhaps, taking on outside investment.
“We’re excited to bring the brand to life and bring the community together,” Zachary says. “We have not even scratched the surface, which is exciting, because we have so much potential.”
